symbols.name: binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of n, rounded up and at least 1, so that lg n = max{ceil(log2 n), 1}.
symbols.quote: $\lg n = \max\{\lceil \log_2 n\rceil, 1\}$ is the base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1.

symbols.name: power-saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^(-182) by which the power of lg n falls below one.
symbols.quote: The constant $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ is the power-saving exponent, the fixed amount by which the power of $\lg n$ falls below one.

symbols.name: big-O bound
symbols.meaning: The asymptotic upper bound: a function is O(g) when it is at most a constant times g for all large inputs.
symbols.quote: $O(g)$ means at most a constant times $g$ for all large inputs.

symbols.name: working precision
symbols.meaning: The number of bits kept after the binary point in each stored coefficient.
symbols.quote: Each stored coefficient keeps $p$ bits after the binary point, where $p$ is the working precision, so truncation rounds it to a multiple of $2^{-p}$.

relations.quote: The time bound $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ disproves the [Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture](nlogn-conjecture.md).

It computes its polynomial products with the [Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplication](harvey-hoeven-multiplier.md), used as a subroutine on packed integers from [signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md).
The power saving follows from [Recursive power saving](recursive-power-saving.md).
The first step reduces the integer product to a carried convolution of radix-$2^b$ digit sequences, as in [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md).
The algorithm arranges its digits by the [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md) on distinct prime cyclic axes.
It computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which expresses each prime-length transform through power-of-two axes.
It converts its middle transform by [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) into a normalized cyclic convolution.

relations.predicate: places its last cyclic coordinate in
relations.quote: It places its last cyclic coordinate in the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](polynomial-ring-y.md), where its wrap is a signed shift.
It computes its forward transforms by [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transform.md), which keep frequency order through their pointwise product.
The algorithm builds each transform level from [simultaneous butterfly layers](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), each acting on one address bit, whose cost is $O(V d^{\lambda'})$ for $\lambda'<1$.
The algorithm performs its address permutations by [fast address interchange](address-interchange.md), whose cost is $O(V u^\tau)$ for $\tau<1$.
The algorithm recovers its exact product by [exact recovery by rounding](rounding-recovery.md), which rounds each coefficient to the nearest integer and propagates carries.
